newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC agrees to cut coffee exports by 1.3 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: ACPC agrees to cut coffee exports by 1.3 mln bags.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) agreed to cut member coffee exports by 1.3 million bags between January and June 1997, its president said.
"We're goin to cut 1.3 million bags, one million robusta and 300,000 arabica," Rubens Barbosa said after an ACPC meeting.
The distribution among robusta producing countries will be decided at a meeting in Bali Feb 6, said the Ivory Coast Minister for Commodities Guy-Alain Gauze.
"We will decide among ourselves in February in Bali," Gauze said.
Indonesia will also participate in the cuts, said the adviser to the Indonesian delegation Derek Watson.
"We will make our contribution, we will take part," Watson said.
Distribution of the 300,000 bags of cuts in arabica exports will also be decided among arabica producers, Gauze said.
"The countries will inform the ACPC secretariat in a week to 10 days of the distribution," said Barbosa. "We did not discuss the distribution at this meeting."

The head of the primary commodities department of Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry, Mauricio Assis, confirmed that Brazil would participate in the arabica cut but said he did not have available a preliminary figure.
"It will be decided amongst arabica countries in the next 15 days," he said.
Under a plan agreed in May, exports by ACPC members were to have been no more than 26.28 million bags in the first half of the year.
In July to December 1996, member shipments were not to have exceeded 27.27 million bags but ACPC figures show shipments of 28.13 million bags, ACPC officials said..

In a statement after the ACPC meeting, the members said they had decided on a reduction in a spirit of solidarity for robusta producers after a substantial distortion in the normal pattern of coffee prices with particular regard to the difference between robusta and arabica.
The ACPC council will next meet in London in May, said Barbosa, adding all future council meetings would take place in London.

The council added that the 1.3-million bag cut would be kept under constant review and would be amended if necessary. ACPC officials said it was possible there would be a meeting of the ACPC technical group before the next council session in May.
